text: Does a Gaussian wave packet v(x,0)=4*exp(-(x+5)^2/2.25), u(x,0)=0 in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system decompose into a soliton train with >=2 well-separated peaks each of amplitude >=0.8 in v by T=6.0?

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing on all nonlinear products (u^2, v^2, u*v) + classical explicit RK4 for full RHS; NO IMEX, NO integrating factor
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 depth=3 synthesis (OPEN) established that Fourier+2/3-rule+RK4 at dt=2e-4 is the working baseline for BKdV at amp<=3, T=10; I adopt this as E1 baseline for amp=4 since: (1) 2/3-dealiasing keeps effective k_max=(2/3)*pi*Nx/L=17.87, giving dispersive CFL bound dt<=4.96e-4, safely above dt=2e-4; (2) nonlinear advection eigenvalues are imaginary and less restrictive than v_xxx for explicit RK4 regardless of amplitude — the kb amplitude-CFL warnings (kb-gardner-cubicTerm-tightens-nonlinearCFL, kb-gardner-G4) apply specifically to IMEX methods where v_xxx is implicit; (3) kb-kdv-noDealiasing-aliasing-artifacts and BKdV-S1 CLOSED entry prohibit no-dealiasing; (4) kb-kdv-IFRK4-blowup warns against IFRK4; (5) kb-gardner-G4-IMEX-CN-amplitudeCFL-blowup warns against IMEX-CN at large amplitude, so I stay fully explicit.

diagnostics.overflow_location: u*u and v*v products, then FFT invalid

rationale: dt=2e-4 puts k_max^3*dt=3.85>2.83 (RK4 imaginary-axis stability boundary): the Nyquist mode has |R|~6.1>1 per step, so machine-precision noise at the Nyquist grows exponentially and overflows within ~3000 steps. The 2/3-rule dealiasing controls nonlinear aliasing (k_eff^3*dt=1.13<2.83) but the LINEAR k^2*v_hat term in both u_rhs and v_rhs is not dealiased and operates at full k_max. At amplitude 4 the dynamics populate Nyquist modes faster than at amp=1.5 (where BKdV-S1 succeeded), making the instability visible before T=0.667.

Single-component change: reduce dt from 2e-4 to 1e-4 (below dt_crit=2.83/k_max^3=1.47e-4). At dt=1e-4: k_max^3*dt=1.93<2.83, Nyquist mode decays (|R|~0.79<1). All other components unchanged (same Fourier+2/3-dealias+RK4). No bank entry prohibits reducing dt; BKdV-S1 depth=3 gives the stability formula.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + 2/3-rule dealiasing + explicit RK4 (IDENTICAL to E1 except dt halved to 1e-4)
bank_use_rationale: BKdV-S1 depth=3 gives the stability formula: dt_crit = 2.83/k_max^3 = 1.47e-4. E1 used dt=2e-4 > dt_crit causing Nyquist instability. E2 uses dt=1e-4 < dt_crit so k_max^3*dt=1.93<2.83; Nyquist mode has |R|~0.79<1 per step. No bank entry prohibits this single-component reduction. No new components added vs E1.

rationale: Perfect mass conservation (0.000000% drift at all 10 snapshots — as expected for divergence-form spectral scheme on periodic domain). 12 peaks with amp>=0.8 detected in v at T=6. Top-4 peaks have amplitudes 3.53, 2.61, 2.27, 2.23, separated by 2.34-14.18 units; minimum top-4 separation of 2.34 units >> soliton width (~1-2 units). The largest pair (x=-3.98, x=11.84) is 14.18 units apart. Phenomenon target (>=2 well-separated peaks with amp>=0.8, mass drift<8%) is met with large margin.
F2 meets phenomenon target with large margin: 12 peaks>=0.8 (need 2), top-4 all>=2.2 and separated 2.34-14.18 units, mass drift=0.0%. No further experiments needed.
